metric_contract.name: Dissatisfied share (bottom-box)
metric_contract.meaning: Share of residents rating a service 1 or 2 on the 1-5 current-level scale
metric_contract.denominator: eligible respondents in the current filter with a valid q9 for that service
metric_contract.null_handling: null excluded from denominator and reported as missing rate; never counted as dissatisfied

metric_contract.name: Missing rate
metric_contract.meaning: Share of eligible respondents with no valid q9

metric_contract.name: Not-applicable rate
metric_contract.meaning: Not measurable: q9 has no not-applicable or don't-know option

metric_contract.name: Problem prevalence
metric_contract.meaning: Share of residents who reported a problem with the service in the last 90 days (multi-select)
metric_contract.denominator: eligible respondents in filter with a valid q4 (multi-select, so shares do not sum to 100%)

metric_contract.name: Severe share
metric_contract.meaning: Among residents naming the service as the most impactful problem, share rating impact large or very large
metric_contract.formula: count(q5=service and q7 in severe) / count(q5=service and valid q7)
metric_contract.denominator: respondents whose main problem is the service

metric_contract.name: Importance and gap
metric_contract.meaning: Mean importance (q8) and mean importance-minus-current (q9) among respondents answering both
metric_contract.format: 2 decimals; ordinal scores treated as interval, use with bottom-box

metric_contract.name: Overall area quality
metric_contract.meaning: q13 attractiveness 1-5: mean, top-box (4-5), bottom-box (1-2); q14 recommend: share 'probably/definitely yes'

metric_contract.name: Sales position (derived)
metric_contract.meaning: Relative sales standing of a district
metric_contract.formula: sell_through_pct < median(sell_through_pct over districts) -> weaker else stronger
metric_contract.filter_behavior: used as a filter; the group tests always use all districts
metric_contract.null_handling: districts without sales data are unclassified

metric_contract.name: Group difference (weaker minus stronger)
metric_contract.meaning: Difference in mean district dissatisfied share between groups, tested at district level
metric_contract.formula: mean_d(bottom_box | weaker) - mean_d(bottom_box | stronger); exact Mann-Whitney U, rank-biserial effect; BH across services

metric_contract.name: Sell-through association
metric_contract.meaning: Spearman rho between district dissatisfaction index and sell-through

sales_position_rule: Derived by this module (no sales target or official weak/good classification exists in the repository): latest cumulative sell-through % below the median across districts = 'weaker', otherwise 'stronger'.

readiness.question: Can we identify weak-sales areas?
readiness.why: No sales target or official classification exists in the repository; a relative split on sell-through across 10 districts is used instead.

readiness.question: Can we measure resident satisfaction?
readiness.why: 945 eligible responses, ratings valid (invalid set to null: 0); synthetic data.

readiness.question: Can we identify recurring issues?
readiness.why: q4 (multi-select problems), q5 (main problem), q6 and q7 (frequency, severity) are present with low missingness.

readiness.question: Can we compare areas?
readiness.why: District respondents range 60-126; project samples are far smaller.

readiness.question: Can we test a service-sales relationship?
readiness.why: Only 10 districts: low power, no confidence interval, confounding by development stage.

readiness.question: Can we prioritise service improvements?
readiness.why: Rule-based classes only; independent availability data exists for 5 of 10 services and no service targets exist.

insights.text: All figures come from synthetic demonstration data; they illustrate the method and are not evidence about real residents.
Highest dissatisfaction: Cleanliness & waste collection 30% (95% CI 27-33%), n=945 respondents.
0 of 10 services show a statistically supported dissatisfaction difference between weaker-selling and stronger-selling districts (5 vs 5 districts).

These data provide no credible evidence that service dissatisfaction differs between weaker- and stronger-selling districts. The cause of weak sales is unresolved by the survey; commercial and development-stage factors need investigation.
6 districts contradict the services-explain-sales pattern (D01, D02, D03, D05, D07, D08); services are not the only relevant factor.

Do not justify service investment on sales grounds from this survey. Ask the commercial module to examine lead volume, pricing, conversion and development stage; validate service issues with availability data.

limitations: ALL SURVEY AND SALES DATA ARE SYNTHETIC DEMONSTRATION DATA. Results exercise the method and are not evidence about any real area.
Ordinal self-reported ratings; bottom-box proportions used as primary measure.
District is the finest area key with adequate n; project-level n is 12-40.
Survey sample is not probability-based; participation bias unknown.
Commercial association uses district aggregates (n = districts), cannot establish causation and cannot be adjusted for confounders.
Resident feedback is indirect evidence about area attractiveness; it cannot explain why non-buyers declined to purchase.
Sales position is derived by this module, not an official classification or target miss.
